title: The old boss calls
text:
[i]“Well, look who it is — my best errand boy makes careers now?”[/i]

Your former superior sits on the board of {studio} these days. He has a project gone sideways — unofficially, of course.

choices.label: Help out — for old times' sake
choices.outcome: You solve the problem silently. He only nods — but in this town, a nod from the very top is worth more than a contract.

choices.label: Name a price

effects.label: Discreet help for the old boss

choices.outcome: He laughs — and pays. “You did learn something with us.”
choices.outcome_fail: “I thought we were friends.” The call is short, the aftertaste long.

choices.label: Let the old days rest
choices.outcome: You hang up politely. Some doors are best closed by yourself.

title: The return favor
text: The old boss forgets nothing — for better or worse. A courier brings an envelope: an invitation, plus a note. [i]“For back then. Pick something.”[/i]

choices.label: Accept the invitation
choices.outcome: A closed event, hand-picked guests — exactly the kind of evening careers are made on.

choices.label: Ask for script access instead
choices.outcome: “Bookworm, as always.” From now on the scripts land on your desk a beat earlier.

title: The old source
text:
[i]“I heard something. Back in the day you'd have bought me a steak for this.”[/i]

Your best source from your columnist days sits in the diner and slides you a napkin with three sentences about {client} — explosive, unconfirmed, ready to print.

choices.label: Buy the steak ({money_fmt:500})

effects.label: A steak for the old source

choices.outcome: She tells you everything — and promises to call when more surfaces. Old networks don't rust.

choices.label: Make the napkin disappear
choices.outcome: You burn the note in the ashtray. {client} hears about it — and never forgets.

choices.label: Decline politely — you don't write anymore
choices.outcome: “A shame. You were the best.” She pays for her own coffee and leaves.

title: The source delivers
text: The call comes at night: your old source has material on a competitor — hard enough to damage a career. [i]“What do we do with it, boss?”[/i]

choices.label: Keep it as leverage
choices.outcome: Knowledge is the only currency that never loses value. You put the folder in the safe.

choices.label: Leak it to the press
choices.outcome: The headline lands. Nobody can trace it back to you — but the town remembers not to underestimate you.

choices.label: Destroy the material
choices.outcome: Some deals you don't make. Your source doesn't understand — your reflection does.

title: The old file
text:
[i]“You drew up that contract back then. You know what paragraph 12 says.”[/i]

A lawyer from {studio} shows up with a file bearing your handwriting — one that would help the studio against {client}. They ask for your “interpretation”.

choices.label: Point out the loophole you built in back then
choices.outcome: You planned ahead even then. Paragraph 12 has a subsection b — and it belongs to your client. {studio} backs off through gritted teeth.

choices.label: Work with the studio — discreetly

effects_fail.text: {client} is said to have been betrayed by their own agent.

choices.outcome: The studio gets its interpretation, you get open doors. Nobody has to know.
choices.outcome_fail: Somebody talks. In this town, somebody always talks.

choices.label: Declare a conflict of interest and stay silent
choices.outcome: “I represent the other side today.” Clean, correct, boring — and exactly right.

title: The file talks
text: The story of the agent who allegedly worked against his own client refuses to die. Your phone rings less often.

choices.label: Threaten a libel suit
choices.outcome: Nothing silences a newsroom faster than a lawyer who knows the damages.
choices.outcome_fail: The threat comes across thin-skinned — and makes the story all the more interesting.

choices.label: Sit it out
choices.outcome: You let the matter ebb away. It takes time — but Hollywood has a short memory.

title: The role that was yours
text:
[i]“We're recasting the property. You know it, after all — you were on the shortlist back then.”[/i]

{studio} is filming the very project your own acting career broke on. The director asks whether {client} would be interested.

choices.label: Prepare {client} with everything you learned back then
choices.outcome: You know every line, every trap, every directorial whim of this material. {client} gets the best preparation money can't buy.

choices.label: Avoid the project — too many ghosts
choices.outcome: Some wounds are better left unopened. {client} doesn't quite understand — you do.

title: A premiere with ghosts
text: The film has wrapped, the premiere is coming. On the guest list: everyone who watched you fail back then.

choices.label: Go — head held high
choices.outcome: You sit in row three, where your name once taped to the chair. When the lights come up, they applaud your client — and a few nod at you. That is enough.

choices.label: Stay away and work

effects.label: Night shift instead of a premiere

choices.outcome: While the town celebrates, you lock down two new deals by phone. Revenge can also be a bank statement.

title: A creditor from the old days
text:
[i]“Without me you'd still be delivering newspapers. Time for that to pay off.”[/i]

The man who lent you your first money years ago stands in the office — with a smile that isn't one.

choices.label: Pay him off — with interest ({money_fmt:12000})
choices.outcome: You count the bills onto the table without moving a muscle. “We're even.” And this time it's true.

choices.label: Offer him something better: access
choices.outcome: “I have enough money. But nobody has ever taken me to a premiere like that …” You now owe him an evening in the front row.

choices.label: Have him thrown out

effects.text: The rise of {agency} is said to be built on borrowed money.

choices.outcome: He leaves without resistance. At the door he turns around: “You know that I know stories, right?”

title: The creditor returns
text: He has patience — that was always his most dangerous quality. Now he wants an answer.

choices.label: Pay him off for good ({money_fmt:15000})
choices.outcome: This time with a receipt, witnesses and a handshake. The chapter is closed.

choices.label: Bring him into the business — a silent partner
choices.outcome: Fresh capital, no questions — and one more shadow at your back. Polite society wrinkles its nose.
